newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end higher on pre-election interest.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end higher on pre-election interest.

text.p: Toronto's stock market closed firmer in thin turnover on Monday as a light dose of Canadian pre-election fever gripped investors despite New York's losses.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index finished up 23.96 points to 6406.08 while Wall Street shed 42 points to close at 7289.
"Despite a rather notable drop in the heavily weighted gold sector, which was down two percent, it ended up two dozen (points)," said Fred Ketchen, ScotiaMcLeod director of equity trading.
Pre-election fever boosted key bank issues among others, he added.
Canadian voters were expected to return the ruling Liberal Party to government with a reduced majority. The Reform Party is in a race for second place.
Polls close at staggered times across the country and the first results were expected to be broadcast nationally starting at about 2230 EDT/0230 GMT.
Trading was light at 67.5 million shares worth C$1.1 billion ($801 million).
Eleven of Toronto's 14 sub-groups marched higher, led by media, utilities, transportation and influential banks. The weak sectors were golds, base metals and conglomerates.
Gaining issues inched ahead of declining ones 463 to 460, while 302 ended flat on Canada's biggest stock market.
In individual issues, telecommunications conglomerate BCE Inc., the nation's largest publicly traded firm, rose 0.85 to 37.20 on almost 1.7 million shares and dragged the market higher.

Steel issues came back into fashion as investors decided the Canadian economy was set to shift into higher gear and would require more steel. Stelco Inc. rose 0.45 to 10.35 on more than 350,000 shares.

Crystallex International Corp. jumped 1.20 to 6.30 in heavy trading. It is in a fight with gold miner Placer Dome Inc. over the Las Cristinas property in Venezuela. Placer shares slipped 1.05 to 24.10.
Grocer Weston Ltd. rose 3.50 to 87 in light trading.
